import pandas as pd


def run(inputs: dict) -> dict:
    events = inputs["events"].copy()

    # Ensure proper dtypes
    events["event_ts"] = pd.to_datetime(events["event_ts"])

    # Sort by the ordering required for sessionization within each (user, channel) stream
    events = events.sort_values(
        by=["user_id", "channel", "event_ts", "event_id"],
        kind="mergesort"
    ).reset_index(drop=True)

    # Compute time gap from previous event within the same (user_id, channel) group
    grp = events.groupby(["user_id", "channel"], sort=False)
    prev_ts = grp["event_ts"].shift(1)
    gap = events["event_ts"] - prev_ts
    gap_minutes = gap.dt.total_seconds() / 60.0

    # New session starts when there is no previous event, or the gap strictly exceeds 25 minutes
    new_session = prev_ts.isna() | (gap_minutes > 25)

    # Session number within each (user_id, channel) group, 1-based
    session_num = new_session.groupby([events["user_id"], events["channel"]]).cumsum().astype(int)

    events["_session_num"] = session_num

    agg = (
        events.groupby(["user_id", "channel", "_session_num"], sort=False)
        .agg(
            session_start=("event_ts", "min"),
            session_end=("event_ts", "max"),
            event_count=("event_ts", "size"),
        )
        .reset_index()
        .rename(columns={"_session_num": "session_num"})
    )

    agg = agg.sort_values(
        by=["user_id", "channel", "session_num"], kind="mergesort"
    ).reset_index(drop=True)

    channel_sessions = agg[
        ["user_id", "channel", "session_num", "session_start", "session_end", "event_count"]
    ]

    return {"channel_sessions": channel_sessions}
